operatingPrinciples.recoveryPlatform: Supabase is a recovery/backup target only; it is not the primary operational database
operatingPrinciples.managementGoal: One private owner control experience with product modules and one service registry

management.releaseModel: validate -> review -> backup/restore proof -> explicit approval -> deploy one component -> smoke test -> observe -> rollback if needed

products.name: Otya Server
products.notes: Do not put OmniPoint operational tables into Otya Server's store database. Browser owner admin remains retired; privileged owner actions must use the protected private owner surface.

products.name: OmniPoint
products.notes: Dedicated OmniPoint API and D1 boundary required. Live schema lineage, tenant scope, balanced journals, provider reconciliation and backup/restore must be verified before release.

products.name: OtyaHub
products.notes: OtyaHub is a product/surface boundary, not permission to expose private service metadata or business data.

products.name: Otya Player
products.notes: Playback, local media scanning and vault access must continue without Cloudflare, authentication or AI availability. Do not upload private local media by default.

products.name: Otya Next
products.notes: Assistant actions must use the same API authorization, actor scope, approval and audit rules as the product UI. Never give the assistant direct cross-product database write access.

nonNegotiableGates: No production deploy or schema migration from pull-request validation.
No remote D1 migration without reviewed target, reviewed SQL, backup and restore evidence, and explicit approval.
No product accesses another product database directly.
No browser-supplied role, tenant, branch, actor or provider outcome is trusted.
Financial writes are idempotent and atomic; retail and agency ledgers reconcile independently.
Provider transactions remain pending or unknown until authenticated provider confirmation.
Recovery is not considered ready until a restore test and safe failback test are recorded.
A green build is not proof of production readiness.
Each release must identify component, commit, environment, migration impact, rollback method and post-deploy smoke checks.
